title: Hidden Costs of the Green Transition: A Bioethical Analysis of Occupational Hazards in Lithium-Ion Battery Supply Chains
summary: The global transition toward low-carbon energy has made lithium-ion batteries essential to electric mobility and renewable energy storage.Yet the environmental benefits of this transition can obscure an important ethical contradiction: workers involved in extracting and processing lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese may face substantial occupational hazards.Exposure to respirable dust, toxic metals, and chemical agents occurs across battery mineral supply chains, often in settings where regulatory protection and occupational health surveillance are limited.A transition that reduces carbon emissions while tolerating preventable occupational harm cannot be considered fully sustainable.From a bioethical perspective, such a transition must uphold the principles of justice, non-maleficence, and respect for human dignity.Occupational health should therefore be treated as a core indicator of sustainability.Governments, industries, investors, and consumers share responsibility for ensuring that decarbonization does not depend on transferring health risks to vulnerable workers.A genuinely just energy transition must protect both the planet and the people whose labor makes that transition possible.

title: Evaluasi Kesesuaian Prosedur Konfirmasi Eksternal dalam Audit Utang Usaha terhadap Standart Audit (SA) 505 oleh KAP XYZ
summary: Reliable audit evidence is essential for accounts payable audits to reduce the likelihood of significant misstatements; the external confirmation method based on SA 505 is one such method. The purpose of this study is to assess whether the external confirmation method is appropriate for accounts payable audits at XYZ Public Accounting Firm based on SA 505. By using interview, observation, and Audit Working Paper (KKP) documentation methods, this study employed a descriptive qualitative methodology. The findings indicate that XYZ Public Accounting Firm implements external confirmations in accordance with SA 505. This includes controlling the confirmation process, selecting samples based on materiality and risk, and implementing alternative procedures, such as making follow-up payments for unanswered confirmations. The procedures adopted have generated sufficient audit evidence to support the reasonableness of the accounts payable balance. Additionally, the auditor assesses comments from outside parties by contrasting them with the accounting records of the business. If there are differences between the confirmation results and the company's records, the auditor looks more closely at the supporting paperwork to find the reason. Since the data is obtained directly from independent parties outside the organization, the use of external confirmation techniques also helps the auditor get pertinent and trustworthy evidence. Therefore, using external confirmation in compliance with SA 505 helps the auditor gather adequate and relevant audit evidence to use as a foundation for evaluating the fairness of the accounts payable balance in the financial statements.

title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ON OPERATING COSTS AND SERVICE PROFITABILITY IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
summary: The paper assesses the effect of digital transformation on operating costs and service profitability of commercial banks. Official data show that in 2022-2024 banking-system revenues grew by 75.8% and expenses by 88.2%, while the cost-to-income ratio rose from 33% to 36%, consistent with a delayed effect of digital investment. A system of evaluation indicators is proposed.

title: Accounting Information Resilience and Economic Decision-Making Extending the Entropy–Resilience Framework to Markets, Capital Allocation, and Economic Shocks
summary: Accounting information is not economically valuable merely because it is produced; its value ultimately depends on how effectively economic agents can use it to make decisions. Existing accounting research has established important relationships between financial reporting quality, disclosure, information asymmetry, liquidity, cost of capital, and market outcomes. However, relatively little theoretical attention has been devoted to the dynamic capacity of accounting information systems to preserve decision-useful information when economic conditions become severely disrupted. This paper extends the Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory (AIERT) into the economic decision-making domain. It develops a theoretical framework in which accounting information resilience influences economic decisions through four interconnected channels: information precision, information asymmetry, processing costs, and decision confidence. The framework proposes that economic shocks can increase accounting information entropy, which in turn reduces the reliability and usability of information available to investors, creditors, managers, and other capital-market participants. Accounting information resilience can partially offset these effects by preserving information quality, accelerating information recovery, reducing uncertainty, and improving the stability of economic expectations. The paper develops a dynamic model linking accounting information entropy and resilience to market liquidity, cost of capital, investment efficiency, capital allocation, and economic decision quality. It further proposes nonlinear and threshold effects, suggesting that informational deterioration may remain economically manageable at low levels of disruption but become disproportionately consequential after critical thresholds are crossed. The framework also introduces the concept of economic decision resilience, defined as the capacity of economic agents to maintain rational and information-sensitive decisions despite disturbances in the accounting information environment. Seven theoretical propositions are developed. The paper argues that accounting information resilience should be viewed not only as an accounting-quality attribute but as an economically consequential organizational capability. The framework generates testable predictions for future empirical research and establishes a theoretical bridge between accounting information quality, information economics, financial markets, and capital allocation

title: PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN AGRICULTURE: IMPLICATIONS FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN SOUTH-EAST NIGERIA
summary: This study examined how public administration shapes the digital transformation of agriculture and what that transformation implies for economic development in South-East Nigeria. Three objectives guided the work: to determine the extent to which public agricultural institutions have deployed digital tools in service delivery, to assess the perceived effect of digital agricultural services on indicators of economic development, and to identify the administrative and infrastructural challenges that constrain digital transformation in the zone. The study was anchored on Digital-Era Governance theory, supported by the Technology Acceptance Model. A descriptive survey design was adopted. A structured questionnaire was administered to a Yamane-determined sample of 356 farmers, extension agents and ministry officials drawn from Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States, of which 320 copies (89.9%) were valid. Data were analysed with frequencies and simple percentages. Findings showed that institutional deployment of digital tools is partial: an average of only 46.0% of respondents agreed that the listed digital services were available, with mobile-based extension (62.5%) the only clearly established channel. Respondents nevertheless perceived digital services as beneficial, with an average of 65.5% agreeing that they raise output, income, employment and accountability. Constraints were severe, led by poor rural network and electricity supply (87.5%), cost of devices and data (85.0%) and low digital literacy (82.5%). The study concludes that the development dividend of digital agriculture in the South-East depends less on technology than on administrative capacity, funding and intergovernmental coordination. It recommends state-level digital agriculture units, interoperable farmer registries, ring-fenced funding and rural connectivity partnerships

title: Trends in 21st-Century Learning Technology Research: Digital Transformation, AI, and Adaptive Learning
summary: The rapid evolution of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and adaptive learning is reshaping 21st-century education, yet their interrelationships and research trajectories remain fragmented. This study systematically reviews research published from 2020 to 2026 to examine the evolution, dominant and emerging themes, and conceptual relationships across digital transformation, AI, and adaptive learning. Using a systematic literature review with thematic synthesis, relevant studies were analyzed temporally and thematically to identify shifts in research orientation and emerging directions. The findings reveal a progressive transition from technology integration and digital learning environments toward intelligent tutoring, personalization, adaptive learning, and, more recently, generative AI and human–AI collaboration. Conceptually, digital transformation functions as the enabling ecosystem, AI as an intelligent capability, and adaptive learning as a learner-responsive application. Importantly, AI-enabled personalization does not necessarily constitute adaptive learning; meaningful adaptation requires continuous responsiveness to learner performance, needs, feedback, and learning trajectories. The synthesis further indicates that technological advancement alone is insufficient, highlighting teacher agency, learner autonomy, organizational readiness, data governance, and ethical accountability. The study proposes a human-centered and responsible orientation in which AI augments pedagogical judgment rather than displacing it.

title: Construction Supply Chain Management for Circular Economy Performance: Procurement Economics and Configuration Evidence from New Zealand
summary: Supply chain management (SCM) optimisation is a critical but under-examined pathway for delivering circular economy outcomes in the construction sector, particularly in geographically remote and small- and medium-sized enterprise-dominated markets such as New Zealand (NZ). This study investigates how SCM practices, such as digital tools, early contractor involvement, strategic partnerships, and reverse logistics, can be optimised to improve circular performance in NZ-built environment projects. A pragmatist, abductive mixed-methods design combined 75 case studies, a 28-case quantitative subset, 15 elite semi-structured interviews and documentary evidence. Reflexive Thematic Analysis was integrated with descriptive statistics, cross-tabulation, non-parametric testing, and configuration archetype analysis. Coordination and partnerships are the most frequently observed SCM lever, appearing in 46.7% of the 75 cases and in all four cases in the highest waste-diversion band, while digital tools are seldom deployed as the primary lever. Two operational metrics summarise these configurations: a Waste Hierarchy Index (WHI) of 77.6%, calculated across the 66 cases with an assignable waste hierarchy position, and a Digital SCM Adoption Rate (DSAR) of 15.1%, calculated across the 73 cases with a stated primary lever. Together they indicate an upstream but digitally uneven pattern of optimisation. The study contributes a configuration-based method for comparing SCM levers in circular construction, together with the first NZ evidence base of this kind, and finds that procurement reform rather than digital investment is the key constraint on circular performance. Practical implications include embedding early contractor involvement and integrated design in public procurement, funding sector-wide digital interoperability rather than firm-level tools, and extending site waste management plan reporting. Priority future research is longitudinal, scale-stratified testing of the configuration archetypes identified in this paper.

title: Prioritizing Green Material Supply Chain Criteria in The Jakarta LRT Project Using The Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP)
summary: The increasing demand for sustainable infrastructure requires construction projects to integrate environmental considerations into material supply chain management. This study aims to identify and prioritize green material supply chain criteria in the Jakarta Light Rail Transit (LRT) project. An Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach was employed to evaluate the relative importance of green supply chain criteria based on expert judgments. The assessment involved five main criteria: Stakeholder Collaboration, Green Construction, Green Procurement, Waste Management, and Green Logistics, comprising fifteen subcriteria. The results indicate that Stakeholder Collaboration obtained the highest priority weight of 21.86%, followed by Green Construction (20.81%), Green Procurement (20.73%), Waste Management (18.54%), and Green Logistics (18.05%). At the subcriterion level, Environmentally Friendly Supplier Selection achieved the highest local priority under Green Procurement (38.84%), followed by Shared Environmental Commitment (37.46%) and Efficient Use of Concrete Materials (36.80%) within their respective criteria. The consistency test produced a Consistency Ratio (CR) of 0.0169, indicating that the expert judgments were highly consistent. The findings provide a structured basis for prioritizing environmental practices in material supply chain management and support project stakeholders in developing more integrated and sustainable approaches to procurement, construction, waste management, and logistics in urban rail infrastructure projects.

title: Why customer knowledge is not enough: supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity as drivers of green product innovation
summary: Purpose This study examines how knowledge-intensive organisations develop green product innovation. Specifically, it examines how external knowledge generated through customer collaboration is transformed into green product innovation, highlighting the roles of supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the knowledge-based view of the firm, the study develops a conceptual model linking customer collaboration, supply chain integration, environmental strategic ambidexterity, and green product innovation. The model is empirically tested using survey data from 301 medium-sized manufacturing firms, analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that customer collaboration contributes to green product innovation through supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity. Supply chain integration facilitates the alignment of externally generated knowledge, while environmental strategic ambidexterity enables its transformation into green product innovation. These findings show that green product innovation emerges through the alignment and transformation of externally generated knowledge, with environmental strategic ambidexterity emerging as its strongest predictor. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by reconceptualising green product innovation as a multi-stage knowledge process involving knowledge generation, knowledge alignment, and knowledge transformation. It shows that customer knowledge alone is insufficient to develop green product innovation unless it is aligned through supply chain integration and transformed through environmental strategic ambidexterity. It also advances environmental strategy research by introducing environmental strategic ambidexterity as a higher-order capability.

title: Strategic Information Systems and Digital Capability as Enablers of Digital Transformation in Indonesian Higher Education University
summary: Digital transformation has become an essential strategic initiative for higher education institutions seeking to improve service quality, enhance operational efficiency, and strengthen data-driven governance. Despite the increasing adoption of digital technologies, limited empirical research has examined how Strategic Information Systems (SIS) contribute to Digital Transformation through the development of Digital Capability. This study investigates the relationship between Strategic Information Systems, Digital Capability, and Digital Transformation in the higher education context. An exploratory qualitative case study was conducted at University PGRI Yogyakarta (UPY), Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, organizational documents, and insider inquiry, and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Strategic Information Systems serve as key enablers by providing integrated digital infrastructure, facilitating information sharing, and supporting organizational decision-making. These capabilities strengthen Digital Capability, which subsequently drives Digital Transformation across the institution. The study also shows that Digital Capability supports process integration, continuous system enhancement, service innovation, and data-driven governance practices. Informants also reported value creation in academic and administrative services. This research contributes to the Information Systems literature by providing exploratory evidence on the role of Digital Capability in linking Strategic Information Systems with Digital Transformation. The findings offer practical guidance for university leaders and information system managers in developing integrated digital ecosystems that support long-term institutional development.

title: ESG SUSTAINABILITY DISCLOSURES AND MARKET-BASED VALUATION IN AN EMERGING ECONOMY: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED NIGERIAN OIL AND GAS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) sustainability disclosure on share price of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria over ten-year period covering 2016 to 2025. The research employed three dimensions of sustainability disclosures, Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) while share price form the Proxy of the dependent variable (Market performance Valuation). The research used an ex-post factor research design, with population consisting of all the eleven (11) listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria as of 31st December 2025. Judgmental Sampling technique was used in selecting only (7) seven oil firms whose report are up to the study reporting date. Data was sourced from secondary sources, since this is a quantitative research grounded on the positivist paradigm. The analysis was conducted using the two-step system GMM estimation technique, which addressed the dynamic nature of firm performance and controlled for potential endogeneity. However, the findings of the GMM analysis revealed that only environmental and social sustainability had a statistically significant impact on market-based performance, as measured by share price. While Governance disclosure were not statistically significant on share price of listed oil and gas firms. Although the coefficients for the indicators of the variables (Governance Sustainability) were having positive signed in the baseline model (Model One) however, the p-values of the variable (Governance disclosures) exceeded the 5% threshold for significance. In line with the findings it was concluded that, high or low levels of information asymmetry do always alter how investors interpret sustainability disclosures. Based on the findings and conclusions, the study recommended among other things that, given the broader dimension of direct effects of the study variables, capital market stakeholders should initiate collaborative ESG education and policy reform efforts to help companies improve ESG disclosure practices.
